title: Jazz did not originate only in New Orleans
summary: Wooding argues that jazz arose all over the United States and that Louis Armstrong became great only after coming to New York with Fletcher Henderson.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Did he say he was from Chicago or New Orleans?
He said he come from Chicago.
Oh, so he'd been in Chicago.
Well, let me tell you about that New Orleans business. Most of those guys -- like I come from Philadelphia, but you hear me talking about Atlantic City.
Because that's where I got my start.
Now, most of those fellows were pure nothing in New Orleans. Louis Armstrong was another one. And Joe Oliver. And Freddy Koppard. They were nothing until after they come to Chicago.
But they were from New Orleans.

Yeah. But they wasn't nothing. And a lot of people get this thing about -- that jazz originated in -- which is very simple and very elementary to say that jazz originated in New Orleans, because it didn't. It spontaneously originated all over the United States. New Orleans contributed so much to it. But even Louis Armstrong still wouldn't have been anything if it don't be for him coming to New York with Fletcher Henderson. Because Fletcher Henderson gave him the showcase. But nobody -- they mention Louis Armstrong being a great man, but they never say that Louis Armstrong was great on account of he come into New York with Fletcher Henderson.
Now, I missed Louis Armstrong by about two weeks. I tried to get him to go to Europe with me.
